newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet, Telecom shares in ratio speculation.
newsitem.headline: Stet, Telecom shares in ratio speculation.

text.p: Shares in state telecommunications holding Stet and state telephone operator Telecom Italia, which are due to merge this year, moved further apart on the Italian stock market on Thursday.

Ordinary shares in Stet were 0.72 percent up at 8,210 lire by 1218 GMT while Telecom stocks were 1.09 percent lower at 4,465 in a market around 0.42 percent down, with both stocks continuing a tendency to move in opposite directions which began in late January but has accelerated in the last week.
Brokers said the market was positioning itself in readiness for a higher share swap rate than had originally been expected when the merger was first announced.

"From what (Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio) Ciampi said yesterday, that the Treasury's stake could drop to 47 or 48 percent with the merger, it's possible to calculate a swap rate of 2.1 Telecom shares for every Stet share," a senior broker here said.
"From Ciampi's words you could extrapolate a ratio of about two to one," another broker said.

The government expects the fusion of Telecom Italia into Stet to be completed by June this year at the latest and the new group, which will retain the Telecom Italia name, to be floated by the autumn.

Ciampi, in a lower house of parliament hearing on Wednesday, confirmed the Treasury's stake in the company resulting from the Stet-Telecom Italia merger would fall below 50 percent "even though I don't know yet if that will be to 47 or 48 percent."
"Ciampi surprised us, as before we'd bet on the Treasury's stake falling to around about 44 percent, with an implicit ratio of about 1.6," a broker said.
But another market operator said Ciampi had only confirmed a trend already emerging in the last few sessions, with selling of Telecom stock to buy Stet.
From Friday's market ratio between the two stocks of 1.71, the ratio stood at 1.83-1.84 on Thursday.
